newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Maranda to list on S.Africa JSE in early May.
newsitem.headline: Maranda to list on S.Africa JSE in early May.

text.p: South African mining firm Maranda Mining Co said on Tuesday it is set to list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) early mext month.
The deal bringing the mine to the market will take the form of a "reverse listing" whereby Rooiberg Tin Ltd will buy Maranda for 84 million rand.
The move still requires the approval of Rooiberg shareholders at a general meeting scheduled for May 8.
Rooiberg ceased mining in 1993 after a collapse in tin prices in the mid-1980s hit the firm. Listed-Rooiberg was placed in the Curtailed Operations sector of the JSE.
However, following the Maranda deal Rooiberg will be placed back in the Metals and Minerals JSE sector and change its name to Maranda Mines Ltd.
Maranda is a zinc and copper mine in South Africa's Northern Province. The high grade deposit yields 15,000 tons of zinc and 1,500 tons of copper annually.
The firm also holds mineral rights over about 80 percent of the strike length of the zinc-copper line in the Murchison Range area.
The group commissioned its second shaft, called Romotshidi, last year and it is now nearing full production. A feasibility study on a third deposit, called Letaba, is also being finalised.
"Maranda exploration staff are confident of finding further deposits," the firm said.
Maranda also aims to expand into the rest of the Southern African region and is a member of a consortium bidding for Zambia's Chibuluma copper mine.
"Exciting possibilities exist for expansion in Southern Africa," the firm said.
